lines.japanese: 今日も俺は柳木原にいた。
lines.english: I was in Yanagihara again today.

lines.japanese: 晩秋の日没前は風が冷たすぎる。今年の冬将軍はいつになく暴君だ。
lines.english: The wind before sunset in late fall was far too cold. General Winter was more of a tyrant than ever this year.

lines.japanese: 見上げれば、連なった建築物の陰影が夕焼け空にくっきり浮きでてる。
lines.english: When I looked up, the silhouettes of the buildings stood sharply against the evening sky.

lines.japanese: アルバトロスの巨大なスクリーンの中では、一足早くパウダースノウが降りそそいでいた。雪化粧のロンドンに流れる異国のクリスマスソングは、よく知らないけど今年の流行歌みたいだ。
lines.english: On the Albatross’s enormous screen, powder snow was falling ahead of schedule. The foreign Christmas song playing over snow-covered London—I didn’t know much about it, but apparently it was a hit this year.

lines.japanese: 午後５時前。通称ヤナポリ広場（ポリはポリスボックスのポリ）に、夜を待つ有象無象が集まってくる。
lines.english: Just before five. All sorts of riffraff were gathering to wait for night in what everybody called Yanapoli Square—the “poli” came from the police box.

lines.japanese: 俺はベンチ代わりのスチールパイプに尻を置き、地下鉄の網棚で拾ったアルバイト情報誌を膝の上に広げていた。
lines.english: I sat on a steel pipe instead of a bench, a part-time job magazine I’d found on a subway luggage rack spread across my knees.

lines.japanese: 巻頭特集は、冬のリゾートバイト。大雪山にかかった馴れ馴れしいキャプションの数々。『グループでの応募ＯＫ』『白銀の世界でみんな仲良く稼いじゃおう！』『キミの冬休みはこれで決まり！』
lines.english: The opening feature was winter resort work. A bunch of chummy captions covered a picture of the Daisetsu mountains: “Group applications welcome.” “Make friends and money in a snowy wonderland!” “Your winter break is all set!”

lines.japanese: 「決まりじゃねーよ。てめナニひとの人生勝手に決めてんだよ」
lines.english: “Like hell it is. Who the hell are you to decide a man's life for him?”

lines.japanese: うしろ頭をがしがし掻きながら、残った手で大雑把にページをめくっていく。
lines.english: Scratching the back of my head, I roughly flipped the pages with my other hand.

lines.japanese: 「なにがペンション住み込みで合宿感覚だ。ちげーだろ、おまえ。仕事っつーのは、もっとこう背中丸めてストイックにやるもんだろ。自分との戦いだろ、あァ？」
lines.english: “What’s this ‘Live in a guesthouse, like going to camp’ shit? That’s wrong. Work’s something you do all hunched over and stoic. A battle against yourself, huh?”

lines.japanese: ぱらっ！　ぱらっ！　ぱらっ！
lines.english: Flip! Flip! Flip!

lines.japanese: チャラついた大学生の横っつらをひっぱたく思いで、俺はページを繰る。
lines.english: I turned each page with all the feeling of slapping some frivolous college kid across the face.

lines.japanese: 薄っぺらい紙にぎっしり詰めこまれた文字。感心するぐらい、世の中にはいろんな仕事があるもんだ。
lines.english: Words packed tight onto flimsy paper. Amazing how many kinds of work there were in the world.

lines.japanese: 短期バイトのページに行きあたった。
lines.english: I reached the page for short-term jobs.

lines.japanese: 俺の理想は即日採用・即日解散、報酬は完全ニコニコ・全額日払い。ひとり仕事なら御の字だ。
lines.english: My ideal was hired that day, finished that day, and paid in full, in cash, that day. Working alone would be the icing on the cake.

lines.japanese: ただし、それ以外は贅沢言わない。
lines.english: Beyond that, I wasn’t picky.

lines.japanese: デスクワークはちょっと苦手だけど、体の方はそれなりに鍛えてきた。同じモラトリアムでも、サークル活動の一環としてバイトを選ぶようなやつらに比べればお買い得な人材だと思うんだ。
lines.english: Desk work wasn’t really my thing, but I’d trained my body a decent amount. Even if I was in the same limbo as other guys, I thought I was a bargain compared with the ones who picked a part-time job like another college club activity.

lines.japanese: 思うんだよ。思うんだけど。
lines.english: I thought so. I thought so, but...

lines.japanese: しかし、時代はアレだほら、あのほら……えー、就職難？
lines.english: The times were that thing, you know, uh, that... Uh, a job shortage?

lines.japanese: 「くっそ、分かってねえ。時代が俺を分かってねえ。こちとら、こんなにも労働意欲に満ちあふれてるっつーのに、時代が俺に付いてこねえ。ああくそ、殺すぞ時代てめえ」
lines.english: “Fuck, it doesn’t get me. The times don’t fucking get me. I’m overflowing with the will to work, and the times can’t keep up. Ahh, fuck, I’ll kill you, you goddamn times.”

lines.japanese: なんて感じでダラリラ、ダラリラしてるうちに太陽が落ちてきて、誌面が見づらくなってきた。もう、こんなに日が短い季節だ。
lines.english: While I lazed and loafed my way through that little performance, the sun sank until the print grew hard to read. The days were already this short.

lines.japanese: 「ハ～ア」
lines.english: “Haaah.”

lines.japanese: ぱたん。俺は音を立てて情報誌を閉ざした。それをくるくる丸めて立ちあがり、デパート入口脇のゴミ箱へ溜息といっしょに放りなげる。
lines.english: *Snap.* I slapped the magazine shut, rolled it into a tube, and stood. Then I threw it and my sigh into the trash beside the department-store entrance.

lines.japanese: いい。もういい。どうせ正攻法の求職は、前後の手続きやら何やらが厄介だ。俺にはこの街で培ってきた心強いコネクションがいくつかある。
lines.english: Fine. Forget it. Looking for work the normal way meant too many hoops to jump through before and after. I had a few solid connections I'd built up around town.

lines.japanese: 知ってるやつに泣きつく、とも言うんだけどな。
lines.english: Also known as begging people I knew for help.

lines.japanese: デパートでトイレを借りたついでに、俺はぶらぶら本や服やＣＤ……それから地階の食品売り場なんかを、買いもしないくせに冷やかしてまわった。あと食べた。
lines.english: Since I was using the department store’s bathroom anyway, I also wandered around looking at books, clothes, CDs... and the basement food section, even though I wasn’t buying. Also ate some.

lines.japanese: 表に出ると、空がいつの間にか海水浴場の汚い海みたいな色に変わっていた。電光掲示板を見上げれば、オレンジ色の１９：１１。
lines.english: By the time I stepped outside, the sky had turned the color of dirty seawater at a public beach. The electronic display read 19:11 in orange light.

lines.japanese: 街にはまばゆい光の花が満開に色付いている。俺は銀世界にたたずむアットホームなログハウスなんかより、この年中無休のどぎついナイトパレードの方が好きだ。
lines.english: Dazzling flowers of light stood in full bloom across the city. I preferred this garish night parade, open every day of the year, to some homey log cabin in a world of snow.

lines.japanese: そう。柳木原の景観は、天井に真っ黒い緞帳が下りてからが醍醐味。そりゃあ子供だって、ケーキに点けた火を愉しむには部屋の電気を消すだろ。
lines.english: Yeah. Yanagihara’s scenery really came into its own once a pitch-black curtain dropped overhead. Even kids turn off the room lights to enjoy the flames on a cake, right?

lines.japanese: それにさ、このぐらいの時間になれば知った顔も増えてくるんだ。まあ、こんな俺と付き合いを続けられるやつなんて、どっかしか変なのばっかだけど。
lines.english: Besides, around this time of night, more familiar faces started showing up. Then again, anyone who could keep hanging around with a guy like me had to be weird somehow.

lines.japanese: たとえば……ああ、ほら、あそこ。交番も近いっつーのに堂々と露店広げてる、キャラメル色の肌をした外国人。
lines.english: For example... Ah, there, look. The foreigner with caramel-colored skin, openly spreading out his street stall even though the police box was nearby.

lines.japanese: あいつはマルチネス。本名は知らない。誰かがフィーリングでそう呼んでるうちに定着してしまった仇名。
lines.english: That was Martinez. Didn’t know his real name. Somebody started calling him that on a whim, and the nickname stuck.

lines.japanese: こんな小さな島国でお巡りさんに怒られながら一個何千何百円のアクセサリーを売ってるけど、向こうではそこそこ名の通ったデザイナーだったらしい。
lines.english: He sold accessories for a few thousand or a few hundred yen each in this little island country, getting scolded by the cops. Apparently he’d been a reasonably well-known designer back home.

lines.japanese: 東洋美術の研究目的で渡航し、民間レベルでの実地検分をするために云々。うさんくさい話だけど、カマくさい日本語でこれは事実なのよと主張している。信じてやっても俺に害はない。
lines.english: He'd come to Japan to study Eastern art and conduct some kind of private field research, et cetera. The story sounded shady, but he insisted in his campy Japanese that it was all true. Didn't hurt me any to believe him.

lines.japanese: 「マルチネス。調子はどう」
lines.english: “Martinez. How’s it going?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～らドラちゃん。ねえねえ、たまには何か買ってってちょうだいよぉ」
lines.english: “Well, if it isn't little Dora. Darling, couldn't you buy something for once?”

lines.japanese: 回転数を間違えたアナログ盤みたいな低音に、似合わなすぎるオネエ言葉。やつは日本語が驚くほど達者だけど、それを教わったのが下町の芸者さんだったって話だ。これはあまり信じていない。
lines.english: His low voice, like a record played at the wrong speed, couldn’t have suited that girlish way of talking less. His Japanese was amazingly good, but supposedly he’d learned it from a geisha in an old downtown neighborhood. I didn’t believe that much.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は血の色をしたビロードの布から、マットシルバーの指輪をひとつふたつ摘みあげて言った。
lines.english: I plucked a ring or two of matte silver from the blood-red velvet.

lines.japanese: 「いらないよ。俺の趣味じゃねーもんコレ」
lines.english: “Don’t want it. This stuff isn’t my style.”

lines.japanese: 「あらやだ、この子ったらＮＯと言えちゃうイエローモンキーだわ」
lines.english: “Oh, dear. A *Yellow Monkey Who Can Say No*.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ、てめモンゴロイドなめんな。つか、俺の趣味じゃねーもんコレ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Don't fuck with the Mongoloid, asshole. Besides, this stuff isn't my style.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ！　二回も言うほどアタシの芸術が理解できないなんて、まったくドラちゃんったら趣味が悪いわね」
lines.english: “My! You understand my art so little you have to say that twice! Dora, what dreadful taste you have.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラはわるい趣味が」
lines.english: “Bad is Dora’s taste.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 台の下に屈みこんで手仕事していた金髪・蒼い眼のガキんちょが、ひょっこり立ちあがって慣れない日本語で割りこんできた。舶来物のお人形さんみたいなゴスロリのドレスも、日本人が着るほどは街に浮いてない。
lines.english: A little blue-eyed blonde who had been crouched beneath the table at her handiwork popped upright and cut in with uncertain Japanese. Her Gothic Lolita dress made her look like an imported doll, though it stood out less on her than it would have on a Japanese girl.

lines.japanese: 「ドラは買えない商品。なぜなら、あなたは持ってない金を」
lines.english: “The products, Dora cannot purchase. Because the money, you are not possessing.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだ、感じの悪りぃガキだな。なに両手広げて肩すくめてんだよ。外人か、てめえは」
lines.english: “Huh? What's with you, you nasty little brat? Quit spreading your hands and shrugging at me. What are you, a foreigner?”

lines.japanese: こいつはアリス。マルチネスの娘じゃない。この辺に住んでる偉い外人さんちのお嬢ちゃんで、まあ、日本で言う鍵っ子だ。ここに入りびたってるのは、きっと遠い異国の地でひとりぽっちが寂しいからだろう。
lines.english: This was Alice. She wasn’t Martinez’s daughter, but the child of some important foreigner who lived nearby—a latchkey kid. She probably haunted this place because being alone in a distant country got lonely.

lines.japanese: アリスは学校が終わると、ランドセルのまま地下鉄に乗ってここへ来る。同い年の友達もいるけど日本人は知的年齢が低いから話が合わないと、おしゃまに金髪を耳へかけながら言う。信じてやっても俺に害はない。
lines.english: After school, Alice took the subway here with her school backpack still on. She had friends her own age too, but Japanese people had a low intellectual age, so she couldn’t talk with them, she’d say, precociously tucking her blond hair behind her ear. Didn’t hurt me any to believe her.

lines.japanese: 「でもな、おーアリス聞いとけ？　俺はたしかに貧乏だけど、テメエの体で稼いでンだ。ところがおまえは、どんだけ小遣い持ってるかしらねーけど、自分ではびた１セント稼いでねえ」
lines.english: “Listen, Alice. Sure, I’m poor, but I earn my money by the sweat of my own brow. You—I don’t care how much allowance you’ve got—you haven’t earned one red cent yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「おうクソジャリ、どっちが偉いンかは分かるよな」
lines.english: “So, you little shit. You know which one of us is better, right?”

lines.japanese: 「Ｕｈ……Ｓｏｒｒｙ，Ｉ　ｃａｎ’ｔ　ｓｐｅａｋ　Ｊａｐａｎｅｓｅ」
lines.english: “Uh... Sorry, I can’t speak Japanese.”

lines.japanese: 「てめ、都合に応じて日本語習熟度、変動させんじゃねーよ」
lines.english: “You don't get to change how much Japanese you know whenever it suits you.”

lines.japanese: 「あらあらもう、ドラちゃんったら大人げないわねえ。軽く流してあげなさいな、たわいもない子供の冗談でしょう」
lines.english: “Oh, honestly, Dora darling, must you be so childish? Let it go. It was only an innocent little joke.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、子供だからだろ。子供だからこそ、大人の誇りっつーのを教えてやらなきゃなんねーんだよ。こんな熊さんパンツの似合うジャリが、大人を笑うなんざ十年早ええっつーの」
lines.english: “No, it’s *because* she’s a kid. Kids are exactly who you gotta teach about an adult’s pride. A brat who still looks good in teddy-bear panties has no business laughing at grown-ups for another ten years.”

lines.japanese: 「黙ってください。私は帯びている、とても優雅そして刺激的な下着を常に」
lines.english: “Please silence. I am always wearing underwear very elegant and exciting.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、私は見せるしてもよいそれを」
lines.english: “Therefore, I may show you it.”

lines.japanese: 「フリーズ！　ジャスト・ウェイト！」
lines.english: “Freeze! Just wait!”

lines.japanese: ふんわりスカートの裾を豪快に捲りあげようとするジャリだったが、保護者の一喝でぴたりと固まった。
lines.english: The brat had already started boldly hiking up the hem of her billowing skirt, but her guardian’s bark froze her in place.

lines.japanese: 「ダメよアリス。こんな若い男が大勢いる街中で、レディがはしたない真似するものじゃないわ」
lines.english: “No, Alice. A lady doesn’t behave indecently in the middle of a city full of young men.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、問題ない。なぜなら、大人は発情しない子供に」
lines.english: “No problem. Because adults do not become aroused for child.”

lines.japanese: 「んもお、いつも言ってるじゃない！　この国の男はおおむね小児性愛者なの。ホラその証拠に、アタシみたいな年増はあんまりもてないでしょ」
lines.english: “Oh, I keep telling you! Most men in this country are pedophiles. Just look at the proof—an old girl like me hardly gets any attention, does she?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、その誤解と偏見に満ちた日本観を後世に伝えるのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, could you stop passing that view of Japan, full of misconceptions and prejudice, down to the next generation?”

lines.japanese: 「それならば、私は願う来てほしいともに」
lines.english: “Then I desire that you come together with me.”

lines.japanese: アリスは片手をスカートに残したまま、残る手で俺の腕を掴んだ。
lines.english: Alice kept one hand on her skirt and seized my arm with the other.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なに。なんだよ。なに引っぱってんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What? What is it? Why’re you pulling me?”

lines.japanese: 「私たちは行くしなければならない、何者もいないの場所へ。たとえばそれは路地裏、公衆便所、そして雑木林などだ」
lines.english: “We must go to place where is nobody. For example: alley, public toilet, or wooded grove.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「私は見せるだろう、あなただけに、とても優雅そして刺激的な下着を」
lines.english: “I will show, only to you, very elegant and exciting underwear.”

lines.japanese: 「んまあ、この子ったらとんだプッシィキャットだわ。アタシもうかうかしてらんないわね、こっちは中身まで見せちゃうわよ」
lines.english: “My, my! What a precocious little pussycat. I can't afford to be outdone—I'll show you what's inside mine.”

lines.japanese: 「見せんな。見せたら潰すぞ。あんな、俺ァおっさんの玉コロもガキの熊パンもいっさい興味ねえんだよ」
lines.english: “Don't. I'll crush them if you do. Listen, I ain't interested in some old man's balls or some brat's teddy-bear panties.”

lines.japanese: 「立ちさってください。私はとても感じた、腹立たしいと」
lines.english: “Go away, please. Offended, very much I have felt.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、言われなくても去るけど、つーかアリスおまえ、いい加減おぼえろよ。いつも言ってんだろ、日本語ってのはな、述語を最後に持ってくんの」
lines.english: “Ah, I’ll go without being told. But, Alice, get it through your head already. I keep telling you—quit turning your Japanese sentences backward. Get the words in the right order.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、これは呼ばれます、倒置法と」
lines.english: “No. Anastrophe, this is called.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。そーゆーしゃらくせえ言葉ばっか覚えんな。ファックすんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Quit learning nothing but fancy-ass words. I'll fuck you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: グローバルな俺は、いつもの『ブッ殺すぞ』的感情をわざわざやつの母国語に置換して伝えた。
lines.english: Being the international guy I am, I’d gone out of my way to put my usual “I’ll fucking kill you” sentiments into her native language.

lines.japanese: するとアリスはＨＡＨＡＮと笑い、細めた目を俺の股間に据え、肩をすくめながら早口の英語でなにごとかささやいた。意味は分からなかったが「アズ・ア・ドッグ」というフレーズだけ聞きとれた。
lines.english: Alice answered with a knowing “Hah-hahn,” narrowed her eyes at my crotch, shrugged, and whispered something in rapid English. I couldn't understand her, but I did catch the phrase “as a dog.”

lines.japanese: 続けてやつの頭上から、したり顔のマルチネスが同じ言語で一言付けくわえた。そしてふたりは、俺の体を眺めながら手を叩いて仲良くＨＡＨＡＨＡと笑った。
lines.english: Then Martinez, looking immensely pleased with himself above her, added a single remark in the same language. The pair inspected my body, clapped, and shared a companionable “Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「……楽しそうじゃん」
lines.english: “...Having fun, huh?”

lines.japanese: 疎外感を覚えた俺は、陳列されていた商品を両手で思うさまシャッフルし、そしてすみやかに立ちさった。
lines.english: Feeling left out, I thoroughly shuffled the displayed goods with both hands, then promptly left.

lines.japanese: やつらは荒らされたテーブルを嘆いて「マイガーッ」と叫んだ。神なんていねえよ。
lines.english: They surveyed the table I had ravaged and cried, “My Gaaad!” There was no God.

lines.japanese: 会話から抜けだしてふと気付くと、喧騒に混じって……いつか聴いた太鼓の音が響きわたっていた。
lines.english: Once I had escaped the conversation, I noticed another sound running through the din... the beat of a drum I'd heard once before.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん……
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon...

lines.japanese: そういえば、そろそろストリートミュージシャンが増えてくる時間だ。俺は辺りをざっと見渡す。耳と腹に響くこのイイカンジな音の出所を知りたかった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, this was about the time more street musicians started showing up. I looked around. I wanted to know where that good sound, ringing in my ears and stomach, came from.

lines.japanese: 儚くも未来など約束されていない俺は、明日を夢見る若人たちの荒削りな芸術を堪能するのが趣味のひとつだった。
lines.english: My own future being a fragile thing with no promises attached, one of my hobbies was savoring the rough-hewn art of young people who still dreamed of tomorrow.

lines.japanese: そびえ立つビル群の谷底、果てしのない天井とせわしのない雑踏と垢抜けない音楽とが混ざりあって生まれる唯一無二のヴァイブス。
lines.english: At the bottom of the valley between towering buildings: an endless ceiling, a restless crowd, unpolished music, all mingling into one unique vibe.

lines.japanese: そんな贅沢がエントランスフリーで体感できる喜びを知ってしまった俺には、もはやライブハウスやコンサートホールにくれてやる入場料などない。っていうか最初からない。まあ、そういうことだ。
lines.english: Once I’d learned the joy of experiencing that luxury with free admission, I no longer had money to give live-music clubs and concert halls. Actually, never had any to begin with. Well, that was that.

lines.japanese: よし、行ってみよう。ロハの音浴は大好きだ。ひとまず職探しは保留。
lines.english: All right, let's go. I loved bathing in sound for free. The job hunt could wait.

lines.japanese: しかし俺が太鼓の奏者より先に発見したのは、道行く女に付きまとって数十秒ばかりのトークライブを繰りひろげる、若草色のスーツ姿だった。
lines.english: But before I found the drummer, I spotted a pale-green suit tailing women down the street and subjecting each to a talk show a few dozen seconds long.

lines.japanese: あの王子様みたいな笑顔のやさ男はプラチナ。仇名の由来は忘れた。やつの好きな香水だかアクセだかが元ネタだったかもしれない。
lines.english: That gentle-looking guy with a prince’s smile was Platinum. I’d forgotten where the nickname came from. Maybe a perfume or an accessory he liked.

lines.japanese: 若干お水くさいナリだけど、もうホストは卒業してる。いろいろ職を変えて、いまはフリーのスカウトマン。仕事内容は──専属契約を結んでいる某芸能プロダクションの依頼を受け、街頭で女優志願者を募ること。
lines.english: His clothes still carried a whiff of the nightlife trade, but he had already left host work behind. After passing through several occupations, he now worked as a freelance scout. His job was to recruit aspiring actresses on the street for a certain talent agency with which he held an exclusive contract.

lines.japanese: ちなみにそのプロダクションとは、独身男性に人気の特殊なジャンルに特化したところだ。
lines.english: That agency specialized in a particular genre popular with single men.

lines.japanese: たとえばピンフ通りの、子供は入れないＤＶＤ屋さんにでも行けば、プラチナがデビューさせたおねーさん達の誘うような笑顔がいくつか並んでる。
lines.english: Go to one of the DVD shops on Pinfu Street that kids weren’t allowed in, for example, and you’d see some inviting smiles from women Platinum had launched.

lines.japanese: べつに詐欺まがいの手練手管を使うわけじゃなくて、そっち方面に興味持ってる女を見抜く眼力に秀でているんだとか。
lines.english: Apparently he didn’t use tricks bordering on fraud. He just had a good eye for women interested in that line of work.

lines.japanese: やつはそんな天職のおかげで、俺とそう変わらない歳のくせに、早くも金には不自由しない派手なアーバンライフを送っている。付きあってる女がコロコロ変わるのももはやお約束だ。
lines.english: Thanks to that calling, he was already living a flashy urban life without money troubles, despite being about my age. The women he was dating changed so often it was practically a given.

lines.japanese: それでも商売道具にだけは手を出したことがないらしい。足が付くところで恋愛するといろいろ面倒なんです。やつは指輪だらけの手で、脱色した髪をファサリと整えながら語った。信じてやっても俺に害はない。
lines.english: Even so, apparently he'd never laid a hand on his merchandise. “Romance gets messy when it's with someone who can lead people back to you,” he explained, flicking his bleached hair into place with a ring-covered hand. Didn't hurt me any to believe him.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ドラさん……！」
lines.english: “Ah, Dora...!”

lines.japanese: 俺を見つけたプラチナが、にこにこと人懐っこい表情を携えて駆けよってきた。季節感ゼロなサニーブラウンの笑顔に、白い歯が光る。しかしこれは羊の皮。
lines.english: Platinum spotted me and hurried over wearing his friendly, familiar smile. White teeth flashed in that sunny brown face, heedless of the season. But this was the sheep's clothing.

lines.japanese: 「どうも。お仕事中ですか」
lines.english: “Hello. Are you working?”

lines.japanese: 「つーかまぁ……就職活動？」
lines.english: “More like, uh... job-hunting?”

lines.japanese: 俺は太鼓の音を聞きながら半疑問形で答えた。
lines.english: I answered with a hint of a question in my voice, listening to the drum.

lines.japanese: 「仕事っていや、そうだおまえさ、あなたの街の便利屋さん成田工務店に依頼とかない」
lines.english: “Speaking of work—hey, got anything for Narita Construction, your friendly neighborhood handyman?”

lines.japanese: 「残念、いまはとくにないですねえ。あ、でもたしか、エージさんが頼みたいことあるって言ってましたよ」
lines.english: “Unfortunately, nothing at the moment. Oh, but I believe Eiji said he had something he wanted done.”

lines.japanese: 「無理。エージの仕事は二度とやんねー。あいつ、ロクなもん持ってこねーんだァ」
lines.english: “Forget it. I’m never working for Eiji again. That guy never brings me anything decent.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、なに言ってるんですかドラさん、あなた仕事選べるほど余裕ない──」
lines.english: “Ha ha, what are you talking about, Dora? You’re hardly in a position to be choosy—”

lines.japanese: 「──おや、どなたかと待ち合わせ？」
lines.english: “—Oh? Are you meeting someone?”

lines.japanese: 俺の視線はあちこちさまよっていたらしい。プラチナは相手の些細な仕草を、如才なく観察しながら話す男だった。狼の目。
lines.english: Apparently my gaze had been wandering. Platinum watched every tiny movement of the person before him without ever making it obvious. The eyes of a wolf.

lines.japanese: 「いや、違げンだけど……この音、どっからだァ思って」
lines.english: “No, nothing like that... Just wondering where this sound’s coming from.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、このジェンベの音ですか？」
lines.english: “What? Oh, the djembe?”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ」
lines.english: “What’s that?”

lines.japanese: 「ジェンベですよ。ジャンベとも言いますけど、聞いたことないですか、アフリカのパーカッションです」
lines.english: “A djembe. Some people call it a *jembe*. Never heard of it? It's an African percussion instrument.”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん。よく知ってんな」
lines.english: “Huh. You know your stuff.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、たまたまですよ。僕は洋の内外を問わずスムージーなラウンジチューンが好きなんですけど、エレクトロなシーンにおいては、すでにジェンベってマストな音なんです」
lines.english: “Haha, just happened to. I like smoothie lounge tunes, domestic or foreign, but in the electro scene, the djembe’s already a must-have sound.”

lines.japanese: やつは涼しい声で寒々しい横文字をいっぱい並べた。
lines.english: In that cool voice, he lined up one piece of chilly music jargon after another.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、たとえば、僕が休日のよく晴れた午後なんかに流すアップめのトラックには、ジェンベをとてもクールにフューチャーしているものが何曲かありますね。よかったら聞きに来る？」
lines.english: “Ah, for example, a few upbeat tracks I play on sunny afternoons when I’m off work future the djembe in a really cool way. Wanna come hear them?”

lines.japanese: 「来る？　じゃねえよ。あたかもバーで隣りの女くどきに入る瞬間みてーな空気出すのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘wanna come’ me. Can you stop coming across like you’re about to hit on the woman next to you at a bar?”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、すみませんクセでして。いやあ、隙があるとつい流れで」
lines.english: “Ahaha, sorry, habit. If there’s an opening, I just go with the flow.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえよ。男にくどかせる隙なんかねえよ。ついとか流れとかで、サラリと人聞きの悪いこと言うのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “No opening. No fucking opening for a man to hit on me. Can you stop throwing around ‘just’ and ‘go with the flow’ like I’m fair game?”

lines.japanese: 「ははは」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 職業病なのか元役者志望の遊び心なのか、プラチナは相手に応じて自在にキャラを変える。それでも、にこやかな微笑だけは常に絶やさない。いちいち面白くなくても笑っていて、表情筋が疲れないんだろうか。
lines.english: Occupational hazard or the playfulness of a former aspiring actor, Platinum changed characters freely to suit the person he was with. But he never lost the pleasant smile. Didn’t his facial muscles get tired, smiling when nothing was funny?

lines.japanese: 「ええと、聞こえてくるのは向こう……ということは、今日はあのガード下あたりじゃないですかね」
lines.english: “Let’s see, the sound is coming from that direction... In that case, I imagine he’s under the railway overpass today.”

lines.japanese: 童顔のスカウトマンは“黄金の右”と冷やかされる節くれだった人差し指で、私鉄の鉄道高架を示した。横断歩道ひとつ挟んだ向こう。
lines.english: With his knobby index finger, teased as his “golden right,” the baby-faced scout pointed to the elevated private railway, one crosswalk away.

lines.japanese: そういえば俺が聞いたのは、この音を生みだす楽器の名ではなく、この音の生まれてくるポイントだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I’d asked where the sound came from, not what the instrument making it was called.

lines.japanese: 「ガード下。はあ、じゃあ、ちょっと行ってみるわ」
lines.english: “Under the overpass. Huh. Guess I’ll go have a look.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうですか？　あんまり近付かない方がいいと思いますけどね」
lines.english: “Hmm, really? I don’t think you should get too close.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで。近くで聞いた方がいいじゃん。なに。おまえ、この音カッチョいいと思わないの」
lines.english: “What? Why? Better to hear it up close. What, you don’t think it sounds cool?”

lines.japanese: 「思いますけど……ええと、そうですね、実は僕の３コ前の彼女が、この太鼓のおにいさんのファンだったもので、僕もその縁で多少は知ってるんですけど……」
lines.english: “I do, but... Uh, well, actually, my girlfriend three girlfriends ago was a fan of this drummer, so I know a little about him through her...”

lines.japanese: プラチナの話にはしばしば“○コ前の彼女”という人々が登場する。数字は二桁のときもある。嫌味に感じられたのは最初だけだ。もはやどうでもいい。
lines.english: Women described as ‘my girlfriend X girlfriends ago’ often appeared in Platinum's stories. Sometimes X ran to two digits. It had sounded obnoxious only at first. By now, I couldn't care less.

lines.japanese: 「へー、すげえじゃん太鼓のおにいさん。太鼓だてらに固定ファンいるんだ。じゃあ、もう路上だけじゃなくて、どっか人気あるバンドのドラマーとかやってんのかな」
lines.english: “Huh, the drummer’s pretty amazing. Got himself regular fans despite just being a drum guy. So maybe he doesn’t only play on the street, but drums for some popular band too?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな感じです。インディーズで柳木原ローカルですけど、彼は特定の人々に絶大な人気がありました。うーん、名前なんて言ったかな……」
lines.english: “Something like that. Indie, local to Yanagihara, but he was immensely popular with a certain crowd. Hmm, what was his name...?”

lines.japanese: やつはスクリーンの中の私立探偵みたいに、人差し指をこめかみへ当てて睫毛を伏せた。口の中で片仮名の固有名詞を列挙している。
lines.english: Like a private detective on a movie screen, he put a finger to his temple and lowered his lashes. Under his breath, he listed foreign-sounding proper names.

lines.japanese: 一時期は役者を目指していたというだけあって、そんな銀幕向けの仕草が意外に不自然じゃなかった。
lines.english: He’d wanted to be an actor for a while, and those movie-star gestures were surprisingly natural on him.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ、ハリュー・クロードだ」
lines.english: “Ah, that’s right. Claude Haryuu.”

lines.japanese: 「外人？」
lines.english: “A foreigner?”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、ステージネームだと思いますけど」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha. I imagine it’s a stage name.”

lines.japanese: 冗談を言った気はなかったがウケてしまった。
lines.english: I hadn’t meant to joke, but he laughed.

lines.japanese: 「で。なに。そのハリューって外人が太鼓叩いてるとこに、なんで俺、近付かない方がいいわけ」
lines.english: “So. Why shouldn’t I go near this foreigner Haryuu while he’s drumming?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はい……ええ、実はですね……その、彼のファン層がちょっと、ええ、マナーが悪いというか人相が悪いというか……」
lines.english: “Ah, yes... Well, actually... His fans are a bit, um, bad-mannered, or maybe scary-looking...”

lines.japanese: プラチナは人のいい微笑みを残したまま言いよどんでいる。
lines.english: Platinum hesitated without losing his pleasant smile.

lines.japanese: 「は？　どゆことよ。べつにそんな、取り巻きの人相ぐらい悪かろうが、俺には関係ねーじゃん。つか俺、基本的に、自分が人相悪いって言われる方だし」
lines.english: “Huh? What're you talking about? Why should I care if his entourage look mean? I mean, I'm usually the one people say looks mean.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、たしかに」
lines.english: “Ah, true.”

lines.japanese: 「たしかにじゃねえよ。そこは否定していいんだよ。むしろハンサムですぐらい言っとけコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘true’ me. You’re allowed to deny it there. Say ‘No, you’re handsome,’ or something, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、そうか、そうだな、よく考えたらドラさんがそんなことで怯むわけは──」
lines.english: “Ahaha, right, that’s right. Thinking about it, there’s no way something like that would scare you, Dora—”

lines.japanese: 「──っと失礼！　仕事に戻ります！」
lines.english: “—Oh, excuse me! Back to work!”

lines.japanese: 「お？　おう」
lines.english: “Oh? Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねーねー、ちょっとお！　そこのおねーさんおねーさんおねーさぁーん！」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, hey! Excuse me, miss! Miss, miss, miiiss!”

lines.japanese: プラチナは慌ただしくきびすを返し、通りすがりの美人を追って駆けだしていった。
lines.english: Platinum spun hurriedly on his heel and dashed after a beautiful woman passing by.

lines.japanese: 見ず知らずの他人に声をかけては、そのたび無視されウザがられイラつかれる。なかなかハードな仕事だ。相当のＭじゃなきゃ務まらないと思う。
lines.english: Speak to a complete stranger, then get ignored, found annoying, and met with irritation, every time. Pretty hard work. You’d have to be a serious glutton for punishment to do it.

lines.japanese: 「仕事かあ」
lines.english: “Work, huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら、職場ではない方向へ歩きだした。
lines.english: Scratching the back of my head, I started walking in a direction that wasn’t toward work.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん……
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon...

lines.japanese: 太鼓の音が反響する薄汚いガード下は、くたびれて輝ききれない白色灯にぼんやり照らされていた。
lines.english: The grimy underpass echoed with the drumbeat, dimly illuminated by tired white lamps that could no longer manage a proper glow.

lines.japanese: 年季の入ったコンクリートは、いつのものとも知れぬインディーズライブのビラと、スプレー初心者の無遠慮な習作で埋めつくされていた。
lines.english: The old concrete was covered with flyers for indie gigs from who-knew-when and the shameless practice pieces of beginners with spray cans.

lines.japanese: 柳木原駅は何本もの路線が集束する一大ターミナル。駅舎自体が桁違いにでかいから、駅前と言ってもこんな風に、区の再整備計画に含まれなかったマージナルなエリアだって残っている。
lines.english: Yanagihara Station was a huge terminal where several lines came together. The station building itself was on a different scale, so even “outside the station” included marginal areas like this, left out of the ward’s redevelopment plan.

lines.japanese: 俺が着いてみると、そこには通行人の邪魔になるかならないかレベルの人だかりができていた。
lines.english: When I arrived, a crowd had gathered that might or might not have been getting in the way of passersby.

lines.japanese: 音の源はすぐそこなのに、半円状に連なる背中の壁に阻まれて、その内側にいるはずの奏者は見えなかった。
lines.english: The source of the sound was right there, but a semicircular wall of backs blocked my view of the musician inside.

lines.japanese: 聴衆は軽そうな女子大生風から背広姿の若いお父さんまで、色々いるにはいたけど、半分ぐらいは若い野郎連中だった。それも、なんていうか、やけにイッちゃってる系。
lines.english: The audience ranged from flighty-looking college girls to young fathers in business suits, but about half were young men. And they were, how to put it… seriously out-there types.

lines.japanese: こういうファッションはなんて言うんだっけか。パンクだかゴシックだか。当人たちに言わせればまったく違うんだろうが、興味のない俺にとっては“奇抜なカッコ”という同一ジャンルだ。
lines.english: What was this fashion called again? Punk or Gothic or something. They’d probably say those were completely different, but I wasn’t interested. To me it was all one genre: *weird outfits*.

lines.japanese: 黒を基調にした細身のやつが多い。あとはレザー。鋲。十字架。薔薇。ひげ文字。両足を結ぶ拘束具。男のくせに化粧。
lines.english: Mostly slim-cut stuff in black. Then leather. Studs. Crosses. Roses. Blackletter. Straps binding their legs together. Makeup on men.

lines.japanese: どう考えてもアフリカの民族楽器なんかより、イギリスあたりのギターを壊して裸で暴れまわるイカれバンドに群がりそうな連中だ──が、これはミュージックシーンに造詣の浅い俺の偏見なんだろうか。
lines.english: They looked much likelier to swarm some crazy British band that smashed guitars and ran wild naked than an African folk instrument. Or was that the prejudice of somebody who didn’t know the music scene?

lines.japanese: 俺はそんな近寄りがたい群集に自ら近寄り、縦に揺れる針金頭とピンク頭のあいだから、輪の中を覗きこんだ。
lines.english: I approached that unapproachable crowd of my own accord and peered into the ring between a quivering head of spikes and a head of pink hair.

lines.japanese: 深い森の奥の林間地みたいに、ぽっかりと空いた半円。黒ずんだ壁を背にしたその中心には、褐色の肌に玉のような汗を光らせる若い日本人がいた。
lines.english: A semicircle opened up like a clearing deep in a forest. In its center, with the darkened wall at his back, stood a young Japanese man, beads of sweat shining on brown skin.

lines.japanese: はあ、あれがハリュー・クロードか……。
lines.english: Huh. So that was Claude Haryuu...

lines.japanese: やつは腰からでっかいゴブレットみたいな形の筒を提げている。てのひらでその平たい面を、踊るように叩いていた。
lines.english: A huge goblet-shaped tube hung from his waist. His palms danced across its flat head.

lines.japanese: 叩くって言っても、見た目はサッサッて撫でてる感じ。でも、そんなんで信じられないようなデカい音が出てくる。もちろんアンプラグドでだ。俺は素直に驚いた。大陸の伝統芸能ってすごい。
lines.english: I say he struck it, but to look at him, he was only brushing it—quick, sweeping strokes. Yet those strokes produced an impossibly huge sound, without any amplification. I was honestly impressed. African traditional arts were something else.

lines.japanese: 熱く響くジェンベ（だっけ？）の音は、俺の鼓膜と腹の底を同時に震わせる。甲高いくせに、不思議と心地良い重みがあった。
lines.english: The hot ring of the djembe—was that the word?—shook my eardrums and the pit of my stomach at once. High-pitched as it was, it carried a strangely satisfying weight.

lines.japanese: ハリューは目を閉じて、古代の祈祷師みたいに一心に叩く。表情は冷たいけど動きは熱い。汗をみなぎらせて憑かれたように叩きまくり、ときおり足首にくくりつけた鈴をしゃんしゃん鳴らす。
lines.english: Eyes closed, Haryuu played with single-minded focus, like an ancient shaman. His expression was cold, his movements hot. Sweat pouring out, he drummed as if possessed, occasionally jingling the bells tied to his ankles.

lines.japanese: 俺は腕を組んでちょっと醒めた傍観者を装いながらも、足元でこっそりリズムに乗った。
lines.english: I folded my arms and pretended to be a coolly detached observer while my feet secretly found the rhythm.

lines.japanese: 仕方ない。イイカンジの音があれば体を動かしたくなるのは、石器時代よりも前から受けつがれてきたヒトの本能だ。言葉を知らない赤ん坊だって、好きなお歌がかかればよたよた踊りだすだろ。
lines.english: Couldn’t help it. Wanting to move your body when a good sound plays is a human instinct handed down from before the Stone Age. Even babies who don’t know words wobble into a dance when a song they like comes on.

lines.japanese: 俺は仕事探しも忘れて、しばしその情熱的な音と姿とを鑑賞していた。最初は群集の外周にいたはずの俺の後ろにも、次々と新たなオーディエンスが増えて、その半径を膨らませていった。
lines.english: Forgetting the job hunt, I enjoyed the passionate sound and sight for a while. I’d started on the edge of the crowd, but new audience members kept gathering behind me too, swelling its radius.

lines.japanese: やがて男は燃えあがる炎のような勢いで音に音を重ねていき、その旋律がついに天に届いたかという最高潮を、大地に叩きつけるような一撃で締めた。
lines.english: Eventually, the man piled sound upon sound like a rising blaze. At the peak, when the melody seemed finally to have reached heaven, he ended it with one blow as if striking the earth itself.

lines.japanese: 一瞬の静寂。
lines.english: An instant of silence.

lines.japanese: しかし、すぐに満場の拍手喝采が薄暗いガード下に反響した。
lines.english: Then the whole audience’s applause and cheers echoed under the dim overpass.

lines.japanese: ハリューは浴びせられる賞賛に一礼すらしなかった。たった一度、ふぅーっと肩が沈むほどの大きな息を吐いただけで、何事もなかったようにさっさと帰り仕度を始める。
lines.english: Haryuu didn’t even bow to the praise showering him. Just once, he breathed out so deeply his shoulders sank, then started packing up as if nothing had happened.

lines.japanese: 演奏は一流っぽいけど、ファンサービスは三流以下みたいだった。へー、と俺は小さくつぶやいた。
lines.english: The performance looked first-rate; his way with the crowd, third-rate or worse. ‘Huh,’ I murmured.

lines.japanese: 例の黒い小僧共は、感動を抑えきれずに奏者へ群がる。口々になにか誉めたたえている。熱心なファンたちみたいだ。ハリューの体から外された太鼓の上に、いくばくかの小銭を置いていくやつさえいた。
lines.english: The black-clad kids, unable to contain themselves, swarmed the musician and praised him all at once. Devoted fans, apparently. Some even placed coins atop the drum he had taken off.

lines.japanese: 俺はあんな無愛想なやつに声をかける勇気はなかったが、数分ばかり楽しませてもらったことに対する感謝の気持ちは一応あった。
lines.english: I didn’t have the courage to talk to somebody that unfriendly, but I did feel some gratitude for the few minutes of enjoyment.

lines.japanese: 財布の中身を確認すると総額４０３７円あったので、俺は黒ずくめの小僧共を掻きわけて太鼓の上に堂々と７円を置いていった。いや、額は問題じゃねえんだよ。気持ちだろ、気持ち。
lines.english: Checking my wallet, I found a total of 4,037 yen, so I pushed through the black-clad kids and grandly put seven yen on the drum. No, the amount wasn’t the point. It’s the thought that counts. The thought.

lines.japanese: 落書きだらけの壁に向かってミネラルウォーターをガブ飲みしていた男は、俺に気付きもしなかった。しかし俺は、街角の共同募金にでも協力したような心地よい自己満足に浸ることができた。
lines.english: The man gulping mineral water while facing the graffiti-covered wall didn’t even notice me. But I got to bask in the pleasant self-satisfaction of somebody contributing to a street-corner charity drive.

lines.japanese: 耳に残ったリズムを連れてガード下を離れる。恵まれない夢追いびとを救済した俺の胸元には、俺にしか見えない赤い羽根が貼りついていた。
lines.english: I left the overpass with the rhythm still in my ears. Having saved an underprivileged dreamer, I wore a red charity feather on my chest that only I could see.

lines.japanese: 宵の口のピンフ通り。おとぎの国から抜けでてきたみたいな全面桃色のミニバンが、今日も道路交通法を無視して定位置に停まっていた。
lines.english: Pinfu Street in the early evening. The all-pink minivan that looked like it had escaped from a fairy-tale land was parked in its usual spot again today, ignoring traffic laws.

lines.japanese: 車体の側面は跳ねあげ式の窓に改造されていて、中にはミニカウンターがしつらえてある。これがパル姐さんの移動式クレープ店、その名もパルクレープ。そのままだけどな。
lines.english: The side had been converted into a lift-up window with a little counter inside. This was Paru’s mobile crepe shop, named Paru Crêpes. Straight to the point.

lines.japanese: このあたりは駅前やメインストリートに比べればクレープの需要なんて少ない場所だけど、こういった商売はなにかと縄張り争いが厳しいので仕方ないらしい。
lines.english: There was less demand for crepes here than outside the station or on the main drag, but apparently turf wars in this kind of business were fierce, so it couldn’t be helped.

lines.japanese: 製菓学校を卒業したあと２年ほど実家近くのケーキ屋で働いてきたパルさんも、ここじゃまだまだひよっ子なんだ。
lines.english: Even Paru, who’d worked at a cake shop near her family home for about two years after graduating from pastry school, was still a fledgling here.

lines.japanese: 近付くにつれて強くなる、バニラエッセンスの甘ったるい匂い。開けっぱなしのバックドアから、三角巾をかぶった頭がひょっこり覗いた。
lines.english: The sickly-sweet smell of vanilla extract grew stronger as I approached. A head in a triangular kerchief poked out of the open back door.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ドラ！　ドラちょいと！」
lines.english: “Ah, Dora! Dora, come here a minute!”

lines.japanese: 女は濡れた手で俺を招きよせる。
lines.english: The woman beckoned me over with a wet hand.

lines.japanese: ドラはドラキュラのドラ。いつだか、真っ昼間からみんなで飲んでたときに、暗くならないと姿を見せない俺のことを、ダンサー見習いのハナがそう揶揄して大ウケしたらしい。勝手にしやがれだ。
lines.english: Dora, from Dracula. Once, when everybody was drinking in broad daylight, Hana, a trainee dancer, had apparently made fun of me for not showing up till dark, and everybody found it hilarious. Do whatever the fuck you want.

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 俺はガードレールを跨いでクルマの前に立った。中から音割れしたユーロビートが聞こえる。何年か前にさんざん流行った懐かしい曲。
lines.english: I stepped over the guardrail and stood in front of the van. Distorted Eurobeat came from inside. An old, familiar song that had been played to death a few years ago.

lines.japanese: 「あいよ」
lines.english: “Here.”

lines.japanese: 女はカウンター越しに手を伸ばし、俺の鼻先にパールピンクの携帯電話をぬっと突きだした。じゃらん。いい歳して節操なく付けまくったストラップの塊が、手からこぼれてる。
lines.english: Reaching over the counter, the woman thrust a pearl-pink cell phone under my nose. Jangle. A mass of charms she was too old to have attached so indiscriminately spilled from her hand.

lines.japanese: 「だから。なんだよ」
lines.english: “I said, what is it?”

lines.japanese: 「じれったい子だね、いいからさっさと出ろっての。ドラが来たら電話させろって、しつッこく頼まれてたんだよ」
lines.english: “You’re a slow one. Just answer already. Somebody’s been pestering me to have you call when you show up.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　誰に」
lines.english: “Huh? Who?”

lines.japanese: 「エージ」
lines.english: “Eiji.”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ……やだよ、あいつに関わるとロクなことねーし」
lines.english: “Wha—no. Nothing good ever comes from dealing with him.”

lines.japanese: 「もしもーし？　パルさーん？」
lines.english: “Hellooo? Paruuu?”

lines.japanese: しかしディスプレイにはすでに「通話中」の文字が浮かんでいた。受話口から男の声が漏れきこえる。
lines.english: But *CALL IN PROGRESS* was already glowing on the display. A man's voice leaked from the receiver.

lines.japanese: 「パルさーん？　おパルさん、どしたのー？」
lines.english: “Paruuu? Hey, Paru, what’s up?”

lines.japanese: 呑気な声は何も知らずに発信者の名を呼んでいた。その発信者はと言えば、しきりに「ん！　ん！」と顎を振って俺に話せと命じている。
lines.english: The carefree voice kept calling Paru’s name, none the wiser. Paru herself kept jerking her chin at me with an insistent “Mm! Mm!”, ordering me to speak.

lines.japanese: 「ったりーな、話すことなんかねえのに……」
lines.english: “Pain in the ass. Got nothing to say to him...”

lines.japanese: 後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら、ピンクの電話へ唇を近づけた。
lines.english: Scratching hard at the back of my head, I brought my lips close to the pink phone.

lines.japanese: 「うっせえよチンピラ。どしたのじゃねーよ。てめえが呼びだしたんだろ、アァ、指名料取んぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up, punk. Don’t ‘what’s up’ me. You’re the one who called me out. Huh? I’ll charge you a booking fee, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、なんだドラか」
lines.english: “Oh. It’s just Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだじゃねンだよ。なんだよ。なんの用だよ、オォ。コチラあなたの街の便利屋さん成田工務店ですが、なんの用ですかてめえ」
lines.english: “Don't ‘just Dora’ me. What? What do you want? Narita Construction, your friendly neighborhood handyman speaking. What the fuck do you want?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、最近おまえの方から営業に来ねーじゃん？　俺ちょっとさ、おまえに頼みたい仕事あって──」
lines.english: “See, you haven’t come around looking for work lately, right? I’ve got this little job I want you to—”

lines.japanese: 「無理」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 俺はパル姐さんの手から電話付きストラップをかっさらうと、通話終了ボタンを長押し。画面が真っ暗になるのを見届けてから突きかえした。
lines.english: I snatched the charms-with-a-phone-attached from Paru’s hand and held down the end-call button. Once I saw the screen go black, I thrust it back.

lines.japanese: 「……あんたね、ひと様の電話なに勝手に電源切ってんだい、ええッ」
lines.english: “...You. Who the hell gave you permission to turn off somebody else's phone?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、切んねーとまたかかって来ちゃうじゃん。しつけーんだよあいつ」
lines.english: “If I don’t, he’ll just call again. That guy never lets up.”

lines.japanese: 「なーに言ってやんでぇ！　そういう一人前の口叩くなァな、汗水流しててめえのケータイ持てるようになってからにしときな」
lines.english: “What the hell’re you saying? Save that big-boy talk for when you’ve sweated enough to own a cell phone yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それよりさ、そんなことよりさ、パルさん俺になんか仕事ないの」
lines.english: “No, more importantly, more importantly than that, Paru, got any work for me?”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　仕事？」
lines.english: “Huh? Work?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。便利屋の仕事」
lines.english: “Yeah. Handyman work.”

lines.japanese: 「あら。あらあら。なに寝ぼけたことぬかしてんだろうねこの子ァ。ええ、アタマ大丈夫かい？　いまエージはね、まさにその『仕事を頼みたい』って言ってたんだよ？」
lines.english: “Well. Well, well. What kind of half-asleep nonsense are you spouting now, kid? You feeling all right in the head? Eiji was just saying he wanted you to do a job for him!”

lines.japanese: 「だから。フツーの仕事はしたいけど、エージの仕事はヤなんだって」
lines.english: “That’s what I mean. I want normal work. I don’t want Eiji’s work.”

lines.japanese: 「はッ、笑っちまうね！　まったくこの貧乏人はマァー、いつからそんなわがまま言える身分になったんだか。この不景気な世の中でだよ？　ええ？　働き口があるだけありがたい話じゃないかィ」
lines.english: “Ha! Don't make me laugh! Since when did a penniless bum like you get to be so picky? In this economy? You oughta be grateful there's work at all.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、無理だって。この前あいつが持ってきた仕事なんてアレだぜ、廃墟みたいなアパートに、ただ一週間寝っ転がってるだけで日給一万っつう。明らかにヤバイだろソレ、なんか裏あんだろソレ」
lines.english: “No, seriously. His last job was ten thousand yen a day to spend a week doing nothing but lying around in an abandoned-looking apartment. Obviously bad news, right? Obviously there was some catch.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみにその前がアレな、あの。指定された日時になったら、新聞紙に包まれた“硬くてずしりとした何か”を駅のコインロッカーに入れてくるっつう」
lines.english: “And the one before that was, uh, that thing. At the specified date and time, put ‘something hard and heavy’ wrapped in newspaper into a station locker.”

lines.japanese: 「それがなんだってんだい。あんたも疑りぶかい子だねえ」
lines.english: “So what? You're awfully suspicious, kid.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ぶかくねーだろ。猜疑心、刺激しまくりだろ。だって手羽先みたいなカタチしてんだぜアレ。あれでアレがアレじゃなかったら、どんだけ歯ごたえある鶏肉だよっつー話だ」
lines.english: “No, I’m not. The thing practically begs you to suspect something. It was shaped like a chicken wing. If that thing wasn’t *that* thing, that’d be some damn chewy chicken, is all I’m saying.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいさね。仕事ないんだったら暇だろ、ほらおまいさん、ちょいとコレ」
lines.english: “Well, never mind. If you don’t have work, you’re free. Here, take this.”

lines.japanese: 女は俺の話を適当に聞きながし、カウンター越しに青バケツを差しだしてきた。中身はガラスクリーナーと撥水剤、拭きとり用のクロス──たしかに、それ以上の説明はいらない。
lines.english: Barely listening to me, the woman held out a blue bucket over the counter. Inside were glass cleaner, water repellent, and a wiping cloth. Yeah, no more explanation needed.

lines.japanese: 「ほう。いくら」
lines.english: “I see. How much?”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、参ったねどうも。前のガラス、鳥に引っかけられちまってさぁ」
lines.english: “Oh, it’s a pain, you know. A bird crapped on the windshield.”

lines.japanese: いくら出すのか、という俺の問いは鳥のフンに呑まれて消えた。
lines.english: My question about how much she’d pay vanished, swallowed by birdshit.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ頼んだよ。水はまァ、テキトーにその辺からさ」
lines.english: “I’m counting on you. As for water, well, find some around here.”

lines.japanese: 女はそびえ立つコンクリートの山脈をものすごく大まかに指差す。
lines.english: She pointed incredibly vaguely at the towering mountain range of concrete.

lines.japanese: ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ、という言葉は呑みこんだ。賃金交渉がまとまるまでは。
lines.english: I swallowed the words *I'll fucking kill you, asshole.* Until the wage negotiations concluded.

lines.japanese: 「毎度どーも。９００円、パー・アワーっす」
lines.english: “Thanks for your business. Nine hundred yen per hour.”

lines.japanese: 「はァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「９００円、パー・アワーっす」
lines.english: “Nine hundred yen per hour.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょいとあんたね、ええッ、しみったれたこと言うもんじゃありやせんよ？　言いたかないけどおまいさん、あたしにいろいろ世話ンなってんだろ？　そんぐれぇのこたボランティアでやったンさいよ」
lines.english: “Hey, you! Don’t go getting stingy on me, huh? I hate to say it, but I’ve done plenty for you, haven’t I? You can do that much for free.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、しみったれとかじゃなく。こっちも一応商売なんで」
lines.english: “It's not about being stingy. I'm running a business here too.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァー、馬鹿だねえ。渡世の仁義を欠いちまったらァ、この街じゃ生きていけないんだよ成田工務店さん」
lines.english: “God, you're a fool. Break the street's code of give-and-take and you won't survive in this town, Mr. Narita Construction.”

lines.japanese: 「でも資本主義ってそういうもんじゃねーんすかパルクレープさん」
lines.english: “But isn’t that how capitalism works, Ms. Paru Crêpes?”

lines.japanese: 「はん、分かったよ。おーし、しゃーあんめえ！　持ってけドロボウ、お好きな商品一枚くれてやらあ」
lines.english: “Hmph, all right. Okay, can’t be helped! You’re robbing me—pick any crepe you want, it’s yours.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー。現物支給かよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Payment in kind?”

lines.japanese: 「嫌だってんなら、この前立て替えたラーメン代、いますぐここに耳揃えて払いな」
lines.english: “If you don't like it, repay every last yen of the ramen money I covered the other day. Here and now.”

lines.japanese: 俺は女を睨みながら無数の舌打ちを浴びせた。
lines.english: I glared at the woman and clicked my tongue at her over and over.

lines.japanese: しかしよく考えれば、それでラーメン代がチャラになるのならむしろ安いのかもしれない。
lines.english: But thinking about it, if that cleared the ramen debt, maybe it was actually a bargain.

lines.japanese: 「毎度」
lines.english: “Thanks for your business.”

lines.japanese: 商談成立。
lines.english: Deal done.

lines.japanese: 俺は空バケツを肩に担いで、近くのコーヒースタンドへ入った。
lines.english: I hoisted the empty bucket onto my shoulder and went into a nearby coffee stand.

lines.japanese: 店員の目を無視して洗面所へ直行、半分強ぐらいの水を溜めてすぐに出てくる。あまりに強気すぎる水泥棒に、気の弱そうなバイトのねーちゃんは言葉も出なかったみたいだ。
lines.english: Ignoring the employee's stare, I marched straight to the restroom, filled the bucket a little over halfway, and came right back out. The timid-looking girl behind the counter seemed struck speechless by so brazen a theft of water.

lines.japanese: ごめんなさい。
lines.english: Sorry.
